issues.quote: Redis has the **AOF**, the append-only file, which it calls its write-ahead log: every write to Redis is appended to the file
issues.problem: The teacher's own label ("Redis's write-ahead log") is turned into a claim that Redis itself calls the AOF a write-ahead log. Redis does not; the fact-check (L-0319, simplified-low) notes the AOF is not strictly write-ahead, since Redis appends after executing the command. Left-as-taught is fine; attributing the label to Redis is not.
issues.evidence: transcript 02:28:51 'So even Redis has this AOF file format, which is Redis's write-ahead log.' / L-0319 (checker note: 'not strictly write-ahead: Redis appends after executing commands')
issues.fix: Redis has the **AOF**, the append-only file, which the class called Redis’s write-ahead log: every write to Redis is appended to the file, and when the cache rebuilds, after a reboot say, Redis loads everything back from it. [[L-0319]] (Strictly, Redis appends a write after executing it, so the AOF is a log of writes rather than a write-ahead log.)

issues.quote: It doesn’t change the ending, though, which comes next. [[L-0103]]
issues.problem: The specified L-0103 inline clarification includes 'Running out of heap does not cause a segfault by itself (see L-0104). malloc returns NULL, or on Linux with overcommit the OOM killer ends a process when pages are touched.' The page drops that and instead says the swap point 'doesn't change the ending', which reads as endorsing the segfault ending that SN-03 then corrects.
issues.fix: One guess is that the operating system moves data from memory to disk to make room. That is closer than it sounds: under memory pressure the OS can page memory out to swap on disk <Cite href="https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/mm/concepts.html">kernel.org</Cite>. Running out of heap does not cause a segfault by itself either: malloc returns NULL, or on Linux with overcommit the OOM killer ends a process when the pages are touched (more in the note below). [[L-0103]]
